mechanism: Nicotine may increase hepatic metabolism of medroxyprogesterone via CYP3A4 induction, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy; additionally, nicotine increases thrombotic risk which may be compounded by progestin-induced hypercoagulability.
action: Counsel patients on increased risk of contraceptive failure and thromboembolism; consider alternative contraception or smoking cessation; monitor for breakthrough bleeding.
